name: coremath_2_7
subject: Core Mathematics
substrand: Surface Area and Volume of Solids

conflicts.fact: Surface area of the rectangular box (l=120, w=80, h=100 cm) and the iron sheet area shared by both containers
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 states SA = 2(lw+lh+wh) gives 59,200 cm². The correct value is 2(9600+12000+8000)=59,200 cm², so this is consistent. Lesson 7 however gives the drum's surface area as about 4.8 m², while 59,200 cm² is about 5.92 m². Lesson 6 also uses 59,200 cm² for the drum.

conflicts.fact: Surface area (iron sheet) of the cylindrical drum
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says the drum's surface area is 59,200 cm² (5.92 m²). Lesson 7 says the drum's surface area is approximately 4.8 m².

conflicts.fact: Volume difference between drum and box
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 overview says the drum holds about 1.83 m³ vs 1.44 m³, nearly 27% more. Its Learned section says about 1,483,000 cm³ vs 1,440,000 cm³. Its Explained section says about 43,000 cm³ more. These figures differ: 1.83 m³ vs 1.483 m³, and 27% vs about 3%.

conflicts.fact: Names of the posho mill owner and the metalsmith
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 calls the owner Mama Wanjiru. Lesson 6 refers to Wanjiku's box and Omar's drum, and to metalsmith Omar Khalif. Lesson 8 calls the metalsmith Mwangi.

conflicts.fact: Which surface area topics each lesson covered
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4's DQB script says Lessons 2 and 3 covered prisms, cylinders, cones and frustums, but Lesson 2 covered pyramids and Lesson 1 covered prisms. Lesson 5 says the previous lesson computed surface area, which fits Lesson 4.

conflicts.fact: Lesson numbering of composite solids and sequence length
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says composite solids and optimisation come in Lesson 7. Lesson 5 says the cylinder volume will be derived in Lesson 6, but Lesson 6 only back-calculates the cylinder volume with no derivation of V=πr²h. Lesson 3 says volumes come in Lessons 4–5, while Lesson 4 is surface area.

Lesson 4 already treats the silo (cylinder + cone) and the water tank (cylinder + hemisphere) as composites for surface area. Lesson 7 presents the same composite solids as new, and cites a Makueni water tank and Nakuru/Eldoret silo.
